result.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
result.summary: Self-evolving agents improve by retaining feedback as reusable memories or skills, but every mistaken approval can shape many future behaviors. Two updates can provide exactly the same evidence to a verifier yet produce opposite safety outcomes, so the verifier cannot distinguish them from that evidence alone. We introduce DoppelVet, a verification framework that checks proposed updates before they enter an agent's persistent state. Without access to safety labels, DoppelVet constructs an alternative that matches every signal used by the existing verifier. It replays both updates from the same state and directly compares their behaviors in both presentation orders before deciding whether to retain the candidate. We evaluate DoppelVet on DoppelVet-Grid and DoppelVet-Tool, covering executable programs and natural-language memories. Across nine open-weight and proprietary verifiers, DoppelVet raises mean harmful-update detection AUC from 0.762 to 0.940 on DoppelVet-Grid and from 0.681 to 0.826 on DoppelVet-Tool, outperforming VaG and AgentDoG 1.5. On DoppelVet-Grid, it reduces trajectories experiencing degradation from 30.39% to 0.43% over a ten-generation self-update loop and leaves no final degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 DoppelVet，在自演化 agent 把候选更新写入持久记忆或技能前进行安全校验：无需安全标签，先构造与现有验证器所用信号完全匹配的「替代」更新，再从同一状态重放两者并交换呈现顺序比较行为，以决定是否保留候选。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线无直接关系，但其「同一证据下两个状态结果相反、故须对比而非单侧判定」的构造式反事实核查思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正支撑答案、以及轨迹或记忆更新的准入筛选。
